Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the statutory reserve calculation feeding Exhibits 5, 6, 7 and 8 of the Life/A&H Annual Statement; method and assumption calls escalate to the Appointed Actuary and the Chief Actuary

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alaska Standard Valuation Law (AS 21.18.110) and the Alaska AOMR at 3 AAC 21, re-read at each year-end close against the NAIC Valuation Manual edition operative 1 January of the valuation year (VM-20, VM-21, VM-22, VM-A, VM-M) plus Arkansas, Arizona and California SVL/AOMR for the other lead states

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly and year-end statutory valuation of every in-force life, annuity, deposit-type and A&H segment: seriatim CRVM/CARVM formulaic reserves, VM-20 deterministic and stochastic reserves and exclusion tests, VM-21 variable annuity reserves, claim and active-life reserves, and ceded reinsurance reserve credit, across 51 jurisdictions of licensure

In-scope systems.value: Prophet/AXIS valuation models fed by the locked policy administration in-force extract through the enterprise data warehouse; segment totals posted to Statutory Reporting (NAIC) Exhibits 5-8

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statutory Valuation Procedure SVP-01 (extract lock, ASOP 23 data validation, valuation basis load, seriatim run, VM-20/VM-21 floor comparison, roll-forward, Exhibit and GL tie-out, sign-off), version-controlled in the model governance repository

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and the Model Risk Manager; re-approved before each Q4 valuation run and on every Valuation Manual amendment adopted effective 1 January

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly reserve close by working day 8 to feed the quarterly statement due 15 May, 15 August and 15 November; year-end reserve lock by 31 January so the opinion can be signed ahead of the 1 March annual statement filing

Deadline reminders configured.value: Valuation calendar tasks in the close checklist fire at WD-10, WD-5 and WD-1 for extract lock, assumption sign-off, model run completion and Exhibit tie-out, with escalation to the Chief Actuary on any missed task

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Seriatim extracts, model run logs and control reports, assumption sign-off memos and Exhibit 5-8 tie-outs retained 7 years from the valuation date, matching the financial examination cycle

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any segment reserve below the prescribed CRVM/CARVM or VM-20 minimum, any unapproved assumption change and any unreconciled extract is raised as a valuation exception with dollar impact, cause and correcting-entry date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Actuary signs off every reserve restatement, prescribed-basis correction and model fix before the reserve is re-posted

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every reserve segment posted to Exhibits 5, 6, 7 and 8 at the valuation date, split by product, plan code, valuation basis (mortality table, interest rate, method) and issue-year cohort, for all writing companies

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Independent recomputation must land within 0.1% of the booked segment reserve; any reserve below the prescribed statutory minimum is an automatic fail regardless of size, and any fail blocks sign-off of the opinion

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation runs quarterly with a full year-end valuation; the test runs quarterly on a reduced sample and in full at year-end before the Appointed Actuary signs

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built, calibrated or run any sampled valuation model

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly valuation test workpaper (population extract, sample seed, recomputation cells, exception log) filed in the model governance repository under the valuation date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Seriatim reserve listing, valuation basis inventory by issue year and the Exhibit 5-8 to general ledger reconciliation, producible to a financial examiner within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Appointed Actuary answers reserve-methodology questions from the domiciliary examiner; Regulatory Counsel clears any response that concedes a reserve deficiency before it leaves the company

checklist.step: Lock the valuation-date in-force extract
actions: Run the month-end in-force extract job for the valuation date across every plan code, taking policy number, plan, issue date, issue age, sex, face amount, mode, paid-to date, status, rider set and account value.
Freeze the extract by setting the run to read-only and stamping it with the valuation date and run id, so late transactions land in the next cycle rather than the current one.
Produce control totals (policy count, face amount, annualised premium, account value) by plan code and hand them to the Valuation Actuary with the extract.
Confirm with the Policy Admin Ops Lead that all pending issue, lapse, reinstatement and death suspense batches were posted before the cut.
checklist.done: a read-only extract stamped with the valuation date and run id exists, with control totals by plan code delivered to Actuarial.

checklist.step: Validate the extract for data quality before it touches the model
actions: Run the valuation data quality ruleset: null issue date, issue age outside 0-99, sex code not M/F, face amount of zero on an in-force policy, paid-to date before the valuation date, plan code absent from the plan master.
Compare policy count and face amount by plan code against the prior quarter and flag any movement over 5% for explanation by Policy Administration.
Write the ASOP 23 data reliance summary: records in, records rejected, records corrected, and the residual population carried into the valuation.
Hand rejects back to the Policy Administration Analyst with a fix-or-accept decision required before the model run starts.
checklist.done: the ruleset has run, every reject is fixed or accepted in writing, and an ASOP 23 data summary accompanies the extract.

checklist.step: Load the prescribed valuation basis by issue-year cohort
actions: Open the valuation basis inventory and confirm, for each plan code and issue-year cohort, the mortality table (1980 CSO, 2001 CSO, 2017 CSO, 2012 IAR for annuities), the valuation interest rate, and the method (net level, CRVM, CARVM).
Check each entry against the Standard Valuation Law in force in the state of issue at the time of issue, since the basis is fixed at issue and does not move with later law changes.
Set the dynamic valuation interest rates for the current issue year using the SVL formula off the Moody's Composite Yield on Seasoned Corporate Bonds average, and record the reference rate used.
Have the Reserving Actuary countersign any cohort whose basis changed since the prior valuation and state why.
checklist.done: every plan code and issue-year cohort maps to a named mortality table, valuation rate and method, with the source law cited.

checklist.step: Confirm the operative Valuation Manual edition and applicable Actuarial Guidelines
actions: Download the Valuation Manual edition operative 1 January of the valuation year from the NAIC and record its version date on the run cover sheet.

List the Actuarial Guidelines that bite for the in-force: AG 33 (annuity CARVM benefit streams), AG 38 (universal life with secondary guarantees), AG 43/VM-21 (variable annuities), AG 51 (long-term care asset adequacy) and AG 53 (asset adequacy where reserves are supported by complex assets).
For each guideline, record on the cover sheet which plan codes it applies to and which model setting implements it.
Raise any Valuation Manual change adopted for the current year to the Chief Actuary with the estimated reserve impact before the run.
checklist.done: the run cover sheet names the operative Valuation Manual edition and maps every applicable Actuarial Guideline to plan codes and model settings.

checklist.step: Load and freeze the company-determined assumptions
actions: Load the approved mortality, lapse, premium persistency, partial withdrawal and expense assumptions for the VM-20 and VM-21 blocks from the assumption library.
Confirm each assumption carries a current experience study reference, a margin for adverse deviation, and a dated approval from the Chief Actuary.
Freeze the assumption set with a version tag matching the valuation date; any change after the freeze needs a new version and a written justification.
Send the frozen assumption list to the Model Risk Manager for the pre-run challenge session.
checklist.done: a version-tagged, Chief Actuary approved assumption set is frozen and lodged in the model governance repository.

checklist.step: Run the seriatim formulaic CRVM/CARVM reserve
actions: Point the valuation model at the frozen extract and the version-tagged assumption set, then run the seriatim formulaic reserve for all life and annuity plan codes.
Check the run log for policies that failed to project (missing plan mapping, negative duration, unmatched rider) and clear every one rather than dropping it.
Produce the reserve output by plan code, issue year and valuation basis, plus a per-policy file retained for regulator inspection.
Compare formulaic reserves to cash surrender values policy by policy and confirm no reserve sits below the cash value floor.
checklist.done: the seriatim run completes with zero unexplained policy failures and no reserve below the cash surrender value floor.

checklist.step: Run VM-20 exclusion tests and the deterministic and stochastic reserves
actions: For each post-2017 VM-20 group, run the Stochastic Exclusion Ratio Test and the Deterministic Exclusion Test and record pass/fail with the computed ratio.
For groups failing the stochastic exclusion, run the stochastic reserve over the prescribed scenario set and take the CTE 70 result.
Compute the deterministic reserve on the prescribed single scenario and the net premium reserve, then set the VM-20 minimum reserve as the maximum of NPR, DR and SR by group.
Document the chosen reserve, the binding component and the margin, and hand the group-level results to the Appointed Actuary for the opinion file.
checklist.done: every VM-20 group has a documented exclusion test result and a minimum reserve set as the maximum of NPR, DR and SR.

checklist.step: Run VM-21 for the variable annuity and guaranteed living benefit block
actions: Load separate account values, fund mappings and guarantee features (GMDB, GMIB, GMWB) from the annuity administration extract and reconcile the account value total to Exhibit 7 and the separate account statement.
Run the stochastic projection over the prescribed scenarios, applying the clearly defined hedging strategy where the company claims hedge credit.
Compute the Stochastic Reserve as CTE 70 with the prescribed adjustment and compare it to the Additional Standard Projection Amount; take the greater.
Record the hedging effectiveness result and pass it to the Chief Investment Officer for confirmation that the modelled strategy is the one actually executed.
checklist.done: the VM-21 reserve is set at the greater of the stochastic reserve and the standard projection amount, with account values tied to the separate account statement.

checklist.step: Compute claim reserves and A&H active-life reserves
actions: Pull open and IBNR claim inventories from the claims platform by incurred year, product and status, and reconcile counts to the claims register.
Compute disabled-life and claim reserves on the prescribed morbidity and interest basis for disability and long-term care, applying the continuance tables named in the Valuation Manual.
Compute active-life reserves for A&H on the two-year full preliminary term or the prescribed method for the product, by issue-year cohort.
Post the results to Exhibit 6 (A&H active life) and Exhibit 8 (claim reserves) and note any block where the reserve moved more than 10% quarter over quarter.
checklist.done: claim and active-life reserves are computed on the prescribed basis, reconciled to the claim inventory and posted to Exhibits 6 and 8.

checklist.step: Value deposit-type contracts and supplementary contracts without life contingencies
actions: Extract GIC, funding agreement, dividend accumulation, premium deposit and supplementary contract balances from the policy administration and treasury records at the valuation date.
Accrue interest at the contractual crediting rate to the valuation date and confirm no contract carries a liability below its account balance.
Post the total to Exhibit 7 and reconcile the deposit-type roll-forward (opening balance, deposits, interest credited, withdrawals, closing balance) to the general ledger deposit liability account.
Send any contract with a discretionary crediting rate to the Treasury Manager for confirmation of the rate actually credited.
checklist.done: Exhibit 7 ties to a deposit-type roll-forward that reconciles to the general ledger, with no liability below account balance.

checklist.step: Apply ceded reinsurance reserve credit
actions: List every treaty in force at the valuation date from the treaty repository with its quota share, retention, coinsurance or YRT basis and its effective and termination dates.
Compute the ceded reserve on the same valuation basis as the gross reserve, and confirm the credit taken does not exceed the gross reserve on the ceded portion.
Check reinsurer authorisation status in each state; for unauthorised or certified reinsurers, confirm the collateral (letter of credit, trust, funds withheld) supporting the Schedule S credit.
Reconcile the ceded reserve to Schedule S Part 3 and to the ceded premium and allowance records held by the Reinsurance Accountant.
checklist.done: ceded reserve credit ties to Schedule S Part 3, sits within the gross reserve, and every unauthorised reinsurer credit is collateral-supported.

checklist.step: Roll forward the reserve and explain the change
actions: Build the roll-forward from the prior valuation date: opening reserve, new business, interest accretion, benefits paid, lapses and surrenders, assumption change, method change, model change, closing reserve.
Attribute every dollar of change to a named driver and leave no unexplained residual above 0.25% of the closing reserve.
Reconcile the closing reserve to the Analysis of Increase in Reserves exhibit and to the change in the general ledger reserve accounts.
Present the roll-forward to the Chief Actuary with commentary on the three largest drivers.
checklist.done: the roll-forward reconciles opening to closing reserve with every driver named and residual under 0.25%.

checklist.step: Tie the valuation output into the annual statement exhibits and the general ledger
actions: Load the reserve totals into Exhibit 5 (aggregate reserve for life contracts), Exhibit 6 (A&H), Exhibit 7 (deposit-type) and Exhibit 8 (claim reserves) in the statutory reporting software.
Run the NAIC blanks cross-checks and clear every validation error tying Exhibit 5 to the Liabilities page and to the Analysis of Operations.
Reconcile the exhibit totals to the reserve accounts in the general ledger and post the valuation journal entry with the Controller.
Send the tie-out pack (exhibit extracts, GL trial balance lines, reconciling items) to the Appointed Actuary as an input to the opinion.
checklist.done: Exhibits 5-8 pass the NAIC blanks validations and agree to the general ledger reserve accounts with reconciling items listed.

checklist.step: Put the model run through change control and sign it off
actions: Review the model change log since the prior valuation: code changes, formula changes, table updates, mapping changes, each with a ticket, a tester and an approval.
Confirm each change was tested in a non-production environment with a before-and-after reserve impact quantified.
Check the production model version tag on the run log matches the approved release, and reject the run if it does not.
Record the model validation status and any open validation findings that bear on the reserve, and pass them to the Appointed Actuary.
checklist.done: the production run uses an approved model version, every change is ticketed and impact-tested, and open findings are disclosed to the Appointed Actuary.

checklist.step: Assemble and archive the valuation workpaper set
actions: Assemble the workpaper set: frozen extract and control totals, ASOP 23 data summary, valuation basis inventory, assumption version tag, model run logs, exclusion test results, seriatim output, roll-forward, Schedule S tie and exhibit tie-out.
Index the set by valuation date, writing company and exhibit so a financial examiner can be pointed straight at a segment.
Apply the 7-year retention label running from the valuation date and confirm the record is searchable by plan code and issue year.
Lock the folder to read-only and record the archive date and archiver on the run cover sheet.
checklist.done: an indexed, read-only workpaper set is archived under the valuation date with a 7-year retention label.

testing.step: Build the population of reserve segments at the valuation date
actions: Extract from the valuation model output every reserve segment at the valuation date with plan code, issue-year cohort, valuation basis, method, policy count and booked reserve.
Add the deposit-type, claim and A&H active-life segments so nothing that lands in Exhibits 6, 7 or 8 is outside the population.
Reconcile the population total to Exhibit 5 through 8 as filed and resolve every difference before drawing a sample.
testing.done: the population reconciles to Exhibits 5-8 with no unexplained difference and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the modelled in-force back to the source of record
actions: Pull an independent in-force count and face amount by plan code from the policy administration system as at the valuation date.
Compare to the frozen extract control totals used by Actuarial and quantify any policies added, dropped or reclassified between them.
Trace every reconciling item to a documented cause (suspense posting, plan remap, off-model treaty) and treat an unexplained difference over 0.5% of face amount as an exception.
testing.done: the modelled in-force ties to an independently pulled policy admin count with every difference explained or logged.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of segments where the booked reserve exceeds 5% of total reserves, plus every segment whose basis changed since the prior valuation.
Take 25 policies selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining seriatim population, spread across life, annuity and A&H.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and covers every material and basis-changed segment.

testing.step: Independently recompute the formulaic reserve for sampled policies
actions: Build a standalone reserve calculation in a spreadsheet for each sampled policy from first principles using the prescribed mortality table, valuation rate and method, without opening the production model.
Compare the recomputed reserve to the booked reserve and record the difference in dollars and as a percentage.
Treat any difference over 0.1% as an exception and drive it to a named cause (wrong table, wrong rate, wrong method, wrong policy data).
Attach the recomputation cells and the table extract used to the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled policy has an independent recomputation within 0.1% or a cause-attributed exception.

testing.step: Verify the prescribed valuation basis against the Standard Valuation Law
actions: For each sampled cohort, read the mortality table and valuation interest rate requirement in the Alaska Standard Valuation Law as it stood in the year of issue, and cross-check Arkansas, Arizona and California for any cohort issued there.
Recompute the dynamic valuation interest rate for the current issue year from the SVL formula and the published Moody's reference rate, and compare to the rate loaded.
Confirm the operative Valuation Manual edition named on the run cover sheet is the one effective 1 January of the valuation year.
Flag any cohort valued on a basis more recent or more favourable than the law in force at issue permits.
testing.done: every sampled cohort's table, rate and method are traced to the governing statute and the recomputed dynamic rate agrees.

testing.step: Re-perform the VM-20 exclusion tests and the reserve floor comparison
actions: Re-run the Stochastic Exclusion Ratio Test for three sampled VM-20 groups and compare the computed ratio to the recorded result.
Recompute the maximum of NPR, DR and SR for those groups from the model output files and confirm the booked reserve equals that maximum.
Check the CTE 70 calculation on the stochastic scenario output by re-ranking the scenario results independently.
Any group where the booked reserve is below the recomputed maximum is a reportable reserve deficiency, not a test exception.
testing.done: sampled VM-20 groups reconcile to a re-performed exclusion test and a recomputed NPR/DR/SR maximum.

testing.step: Test the ceded reinsurance reserve credit and its collateral
actions: Select the five largest ceded treaties by reserve credit and read the treaty terms in the treaty repository for quota share, retention and coinsurance basis.
Recompute the ceded reserve on the gross valuation basis and compare to the credit taken in Schedule S Part 3.
For every unauthorised or certified reinsurer, obtain the letter of credit, trust statement or funds withheld balance at the valuation date and confirm it covers the credit.
Treat any credit exceeding the recomputed ceded reserve or lacking collateral as an exception with the dollar amount stated.
testing.done: sampled ceded credits agree to a recomputed ceded reserve and every unauthorised-reinsurer credit is fully collateralised.

testing.step: Recompute the roll-forward and the exhibit-to-ledger tie
actions: Recompute the reserve roll-forward from the prior filed Exhibit 5 to the current one using independently obtained new business, benefit and surrender data.
Compare each attribution line to the Analysis of Increase in Reserves exhibit and quantify any residual.
Trace the closing reserve to the general ledger reserve account balances and to the valuation journal entry, checking the entry date falls inside the close window.
Flag any reconciling item held open from a prior quarter as an aged exception.
testing.done: the roll-forward, the Analysis of Increase in Reserves and the general ledger reserve accounts agree with no aged open items.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each exception with the segment, the dollar impact, the affected exhibit and whether the booked reserve was understated.
Assign a root cause (data extract gap, wrong prescribed basis, unapproved assumption, model version drift, reinsurance credit error) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date inside the current close where the reserve is understated, and notify the Appointed Actuary immediately so the opinion is not signed over a known deficiency.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment, with understatements escalated to the Appointed Actuary.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the valuation test
actions: Compute the exception rate and the aggregate dollar impact against the 0.1% recomputation tolerance and the zero-tolerance minimum-reserve threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with a direct reference to each supporting workpaper section.
Have the independent reviewer, who built and ran none of the sampled models, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any reserve deficiency to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception rate, the dollar impact and a conclusion, and the Audit Committee reporting date is recorded.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Signs the Statement of Actuarial Opinion in a personal professional capacity and owns the supporting Actuarial Memorandum and the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — VM-30 of the operative Valuation Manual (prescribed opinion wording, memorandum and RAAIS content), the Alaska AOMR at 3 AAC 21 and AS 21.18, plus ASOP 22, ASOP 7 and ASOP 41, re-read before drafting each year's opinion

In-scope processes.value: Annual opinion cycle for each writing company: appointment confirmation, qualification attestation, scope definition, reliance collection, opinion drafting on the prescribed VM-30 wording, memorandum and RAAIS drafting, peer review, board reporting and signature

In-scope systems.value: Opinion, memorandum and RAAIS drafted and version-controlled in the document repository; the signed PDF is handed to Statutory Reporting (NAIC) for attachment to the annual statement

Compliance procedure documented.value: Actuarial Opinion Procedure AOP-01 — appointment and qualification evidence, scope and reliance matrix, prescribed wording control, opinion-type decision tree, memorandum table of contents mapped to VM-30 Section 3.D, peer review and signature

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and reviewed by the Audit Committee each year before the opinion cycle opens; re-approved on any VM-30 wording change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Opinion signed and dated before the 1 March annual statement filing; RAAIS filed with the domiciliary commissioner by 15 March; Actuarial Memorandum completed and available by 31 December of the year following the valuation date and delivered within 30 days of any commissioner request

Deadline reminders configured.value: Opinion calendar alerts at 15 January (draft due), 10 February (peer review complete), 25 February (signature) and 10 March (RAAIS lodged), with escalation to the Chief Financial Officer on slippage

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed opinion, memorandum, RAAIS, board appointment resolution, qualification attestation and every reliance statement retained 7 years from the valuation date under a confidential-actuarial label

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A qualified, adverse or inconclusive opinion, a missing reliance statement, or a memorandum not complete by the 31 December deadline is logged as a regulatory exception with the disclosure made and the remediation owner

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Actuary signs off any change to opinion type, any re-issued opinion and any late memorandum, and reports it to the Audit Committee

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every Statement of Actuarial Opinion required for the valuation year, one per writing company, together with its memorandum, RAAIS and the reliance statements behind it

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — an opinion signed without a valid appointment, without a current qualification attestation, without every required reliance statement, or departing from the prescribed VM-30 wording without disclosure is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs once per valuation year on 100% of opinions, executed between the draft and the signature date so findings can still be corrected

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must be outside the actuarial reporting line and must not have drafted or peer-reviewed the opinion

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual opinion review workpaper (wording comparison, reliance matrix, qualification file, trace to valuation workpapers) in the compliance evidence repository under the valuation year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed opinion, memorandum, RAAIS, board resolution and reliance statements assembled as one examination pack, producible to the Alaska Division of Insurance within 30 days of request

Regulator response path.value: Appointed Actuary responds personally on opinion content; Regulatory Counsel handles confidentiality assertions over the memorandum and RAAIS before anything is released

checklist.step: Confirm the Appointed Actuary appointment is live and notified
actions: Pull the board resolution from the board portal that appoints the actuary, and confirm it names the individual, the effective date and the companies covered.
Confirm the domiciliary commissioner was notified of the appointment within 5 business days of the board action, and file the acknowledgement.

Where an actuary was replaced during the year, confirm the notification within 5 business days plus the separate letter within 10 business days stating whether there were disagreements over reserves, and file both.
Hand the resolution and notification file to the Appointed Actuary for the opinion evidence pack.
checklist.done: a current board resolution and a dated commissioner notification exist for every company covered by the opinion.

checklist.step: Evidence the qualified-actuary requirement
actions: Attach the current American Academy of Actuaries membership confirmation and the Member Identification Number to the evidence pack.
Attach the signed attestation of compliance with the US Qualification Standards, including the Specific Qualification Standard for statements of actuarial opinion on life and health reserves.
Attach the continuing education log for the year showing at least 30 hours with the required relevant and professionalism content, itemised by activity and date.
Confirm in writing that no disqualification event under the AOMR (regulatory action, felony, prior opinion rejection) applies.
checklist.done: membership, a signed qualification attestation, a compliant CE log and a no-disqualification statement are on file.

checklist.step: Fix the scope of the opinion against the annual statement
actions: List every liability item the opinion will cover with its exhibit and page reference: Exhibit 5 aggregate reserve for life contracts, Exhibit 6 A&H, Exhibit 7 deposit-type contracts, Exhibit 8 claim reserves, and the related actuarial items on the Liabilities page.
Name explicitly anything excluded from asset adequacy analysis and state the basis for exclusion.
Take the booked amount for each scoped item from the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) exhibit extract and record it in the scope table so the opinion quotes filed figures.
Have the Statutory Reporting Manager confirm the scope table matches the statement as it will be filed.
checklist.done: a scope table lists every opinion item with its exhibit, page reference and filed amount, confirmed by Statutory Reporting.

checklist.step: Collect the officer reliance statement on data
actions: Draft the reliance statement for signature by the officer responsible for the in-force records, naming the extract, the valuation date and the records covered.
Have the officer confirm the data are substantially accurate and complete, and that the listings reconcile to the annual statement.
Attach the ASOP 23 data quality summary produced by the Data Quality Analyst so the reliance is supported rather than bare.
Return the signed, dated statement to the Appointed Actuary before the opinion is drafted, not after.
checklist.done: a signed, dated officer reliance statement on data exists, supported by the ASOP 23 data summary.

checklist.step: Collect the remaining reliance statements
actions: Obtain a reliance statement from the Chief Investment Officer covering asset data, cash flow characteristics and the investment strategy modelled in asset adequacy analysis.
Obtain a reliance statement from any other actuary whose work is relied on, naming the block, the work relied on and that actuary's qualification.
Obtain a reliance statement covering reinsurance treaty terms from the Reinsurance Manager where treaty interpretation drives the reserve credit.
Build a reliance matrix listing each reliance, the signer, the date and the opinion paragraph it supports, and treat any missing signature as a blocker to signature.
checklist.done: a reliance matrix shows a signed, dated statement behind every reliance the opinion will assert.

checklist.step: Take in the asset adequacy conclusion and the additional reserve, if any
actions: Hand the Appointed Actuary the asset adequacy results by block: scenario set used, results under each deterministic scenario, the stochastic measure, and the aggregate surplus position at the end of the projection.
State whether reserves make good and sufficient provision under moderately adverse conditions, and quantify any additional reserve required.
Where an additional reserve is needed, agree the amount with the Chief Actuary and hand the booking instruction to the Statutory Reporting Manager before the statement is finalised.
Provide the AG 53 and AG 51 conclusions separately where complex assets or long-term care business is in scope.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary holds a written asset adequacy conclusion by block, with any additional reserve quantified and booked.

checklist.step: Draft the opinion on the prescribed VM-30 wording
actions: Start from the current VM-30 Section 3 prescribed opinion template rather than last year's document, and diff the two to catch wording changes.

Complete the identification paragraph (appointment, appointing body, date of appointment, qualification), the scoping paragraph (the scope table items), the reliance paragraph (naming each reliance) and the opinion paragraph.

Confirm the opinion paragraph asserts the reserves meet the requirements of the laws of the state of domicile, are computed on the stated basis, are at least as great as the minimum required by every state in which the statement is filed, and make good and sufficient provision.
Redline any departure from the prescribed wording and record why it is needed, since undisclosed departures are the most common examination finding.
checklist.done: the draft opinion follows the current VM-30 prescribed wording with every departure redlined and justified.

checklist.step: Determine the opinion type and draft the relevant comment paragraphs
actions: Apply the decision tree: unqualified where all scoped reserves are adequate; qualified where one or more items is excluded or unresolved; adverse where reserves are not adequate; inconclusive where the analysis could not be completed.

Draft relevant comment paragraphs for anything a regulator would want flagged: material reinsurance ceded to an affiliate or unauthorised reinsurer, AG 53 complex asset reliance, AG 38 secondary guarantee reserves, LTC morbidity, a material assumption change, or a reserve method change.
Where the opinion is other than unqualified, notify the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Risk Officer the same day and prepare for the regulator conversation that follows.
Record the opinion-type decision and its basis on the opinion decision sheet.
checklist.done: the opinion type is set with a documented basis and every material issue has a relevant comment paragraph.

checklist.step: Draft the Actuarial Memorandum to the VM-30 content list
actions: Build the memorandum against the VM-30 Section 3.D content list so no required section is missing: purpose and scope, description of the business, reserve methods and bases, asset portfolio and investment strategy, assumptions with rationale and margins, scenarios tested, results, sensitivity tests, reinsurance treatment, and the conclusion.
Cross-reference each section to the valuation workpaper or asset adequacy exhibit that supports it so the memorandum is navigable during an examination.
Include the summary of material changes from the prior year memorandum, including assumption, method and model changes with their reserve impact.
Mark every page confidential under the AOMR confidentiality provision and record the completion date against the 31 December of the following year deadline.
checklist.done: the memorandum covers every VM-30 Section 3.D section, cross-references its support and is dated inside the required completion window.

checklist.step: Draft the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary
actions: Summarise the material risks and the blocks driving them, the scenarios producing negative ending surplus, and how many of the prescribed deterministic scenarios failed.
Compare this year's results to the prior year and explain material movements in the aggregate surplus position.
State the extent to which the analysis relied on aggregation across blocks and the effect of removing that aggregation.
Include the Appointed Actuary's comments on any reserve item where the margin is thin, and prepare it for filing with the domiciliary commissioner by 15 March.
checklist.done: a RAAIS covering material risks, failing scenarios, prior-year comparison and aggregation effects is ready ahead of 15 March.

checklist.step: Put the opinion and memorandum through peer review
actions: Assign a reviewer who did not prepare the opinion or run the asset adequacy models and give them the full evidence pack.

Reviewer checks the prescribed wording line by line, traces every number in the opinion to the scope table and the valuation workpapers, and tests the opinion-type conclusion against the asset adequacy results.
Reviewer records comments and their disposition on a review sheet; unresolved comments block signature.
Chief Actuary signs the review sheet confirming peer review is complete before the opinion goes to the board.
checklist.done: a completed peer review sheet with every comment dispositioned is signed by the Chief Actuary before signature.

checklist.step: Report the opinion to the board and the audit committee
actions: Table the draft opinion, the asset adequacy conclusion and any additional reserve at the audit committee meeting held before the 1 March filing.
Present the opinion type, the relevant comment paragraphs and the year-on-year movement in the aggregate surplus position.
Record the committee's acknowledgement in the minutes, noting that the opinion is the Appointed Actuary's professional statement and is not subject to management amendment.
Upload the minutes extract to the opinion evidence pack.
checklist.done: the audit committee has been shown the opinion and any additional reserve, with the minutes extract filed in the evidence pack.

checklist.step: Sign and date the opinion
actions: Confirm the reliance matrix is complete, the peer review sheet is signed, and the exhibit amounts in the scope table match the statement about to be filed.
Sign the opinion with name, title, employer or firm, address, telephone number and email as the prescribed wording requires, and date it on or before the statement filing date.
Produce a text-searchable PDF of the signed opinion and hand it to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for attachment to the annual statement.
Refuse to sign where any reliance is missing or any scoped reserve is unresolved, and escalate to the Chief Financial Officer the same day.
checklist.done: a signed, dated opinion PDF carrying full signatory details is in the hands of Regulatory Reporting before the filing run.

checklist.step: Log the opinion in the regulatory obligation register
actions: Create the register entry for the valuation year with company, opinion type, signature date, memorandum completion date and RAAIS filing date.
Set the tracker milestones for the 15 March RAAIS filing and the 31 December memorandum availability date, with reminders 30 days ahead of each.
Link the entry to the opinion evidence pack so any regulator request resolves in one hop.
Flag any qualified, adverse or inconclusive opinion as an open regulatory issue with an assigned owner.
checklist.done: the register holds a linked entry per company with signature, RAAIS and memorandum milestones and reminders armed.

checklist.step: Archive the opinion evidence pack under confidentiality controls
actions: Assemble the pack: signed opinion, memorandum, RAAIS, board resolution and commissioner notification, qualification attestation and CE log, reliance matrix and statements, peer review sheet, scope table and audit committee minutes extract.
Apply the confidential-actuarial access label so the memorandum and RAAIS are restricted to Actuarial, Regulatory Counsel and named examiners.
Apply the 7-year retention label running from the valuation date.
Confirm the pack is indexed by valuation year and writing company and record the archive date.
checklist.done: a complete, access-restricted opinion pack is archived and indexed by valuation year and writing company.

testing.step: Build the population of opinions required for the valuation year
actions: List every legal entity that files a life or A&H annual statement, from the corporate entity register and the NAIC company codes on the jurat pages.
Confirm each entity requires a Statement of Actuarial Opinion for the valuation year and note any entity claiming an exemption with the basis.
Reconcile the list to the opinions actually produced and treat any entity without an opinion as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every statement-filing entity is matched to a required opinion or a documented exemption.

testing.step: Reconcile the opinion scope to the filed annual statement
actions: Take the scope table amounts quoted in each opinion and compare them line by line to Exhibits 5, 6, 7 and 8 and the Liabilities page as filed.
Confirm no actuarial liability on the Liabilities page sits outside both the opinion scope and the stated exclusions.
Quantify any difference between the opinion figure and the filed figure and treat any difference at all as an exception, since the opinion must quote filed amounts.
testing.done: every opinion amount agrees to the filed exhibit and no actuarial liability is unscoped and undisclosed.

testing.step: Draw the sample of opinion paragraphs and supporting items
actions: Take 100% of opinions, since the population is one per writing company.
Within each opinion, select every relevant comment paragraph, every reliance asserted, and the three largest scoped reserve items for tracing.
Record the selection basis and date in the workpaper so the review can be repeated.
testing.done: the sample covers all opinions, all relevant comments, all reliances and the three largest reserve items each, with the basis recorded.

testing.step: Compare the opinion wording to the prescribed VM-30 text
actions: Download the VM-30 Section 3 prescribed opinion wording from the Valuation Manual edition operative for the valuation year.
Run a clause-by-clause comparison against the signed opinion covering the identification, scoping, reliance and opinion paragraphs.
Confirm the opinion asserts adequacy under the law of the state of domicile and that reserves meet the minimum of every state in which the statement is filed.
Treat any wording departure not redlined and justified on the decision sheet as a fail, not a drafting preference.
testing.done: each opinion is clause-matched to the operative prescribed wording with every departure justified in writing.

testing.step: Re-perform the qualified-actuary and appointment checks
actions: Verify Academy membership independently and check the Member Identification Number against the Academy directory.
Recount the continuing education log against the 30-hour requirement and check the relevant and professionalism content split, rejecting undated or unattributed entries.
Read the board resolution and confirm the appointment covers the valuation year and the entity signing the opinion.
Recompute the commissioner notification date against the 5 business day requirement from the board action date.
testing.done: membership, CE hours, appointment coverage and the 5-business-day notification are independently verified.

testing.step: Test the reliance matrix for completeness and date order
actions: Pull every reliance asserted in the opinion text and match it to a signed statement in the evidence pack.
Check each statement is signed by the correct role, names the specific data or work relied on, and is dated on or before the opinion signature date.
Confirm the officer data reliance is supported by the ASOP 23 data quality summary rather than a bare assertion.
Treat a reliance asserted with no signed statement, or one dated after signature, as an automatic fail.
testing.done: every asserted reliance has a correctly signed statement dated on or before the opinion date.

testing.step: Trace opinion and memorandum figures back to the valuation workpapers
actions: For the three largest scoped reserve items per opinion, trace the quoted amount to the valuation model output and the exhibit tie-out in the model governance repository.
Trace the additional reserve, where one was booked, to the asset adequacy conclusion memo and to the journal entry posted by the Controller.
Check the memorandum's summary of material changes agrees to the model change log and the assumption version history.
Flag any figure in the opinion or memorandum with no traceable workpaper support.
testing.done: every traced figure resolves to a dated workpaper, model output or journal entry.

testing.step: Recompute the memorandum and RAAIS deadline maths
actions: Confirm the opinion signature date is on or before the 1 March annual statement filing date for each entity.
Confirm the RAAIS filing date with the domiciliary commissioner is on or before 15 March and that a confirmation exists.
Confirm the memorandum completion date is on or before 31 December of the year following the valuation date, and that any commissioner request during the year was answered within 30 days.
Record each date and its evidence reference, and log any breach with the number of days late.
testing.done: the 1 March, 15 March, 31 December and 30-day request deadlines are each evidenced or logged as a dated breach.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the entity, the opinion element affected and whether the defect is visible on the face of the filed opinion.
Assign a root cause (stale wording template, missing reliance, late memorandum, expired qualification, unscoped liability) and a named owner.
Where the defect is on the face of a filed opinion, open a re-issue assessment with Regulatory Counsel and set the remediation date inside 30 days.
Carry every open exception into next year's opinion cycle as a mandatory pre-signature check.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a next-cycle pre-signature check.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the opinion review
actions: Compute the exception count against the zero-tolerance threshold for appointment, qualification, reliance and prescribed wording defects.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with a reference to each supporting workpaper section.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither drafted nor peer-reviewed the opinion, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any qualified, adverse or inconclusive opinion to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception count and a conclusion, with the Audit Committee reporting date recorded.

checklist.step: Build the jurisdiction filing matrix for the valuation year
actions: List every writing company against every state where it holds a certificate of authority, taking the licence list from the company licence register and the NAIC company codes from the jurat page.
For each row record the filing method (NAIC electronic only, state portal, hard copy), whether the state requires an original signed opinion, the filing fee and the payment method.
Pull each state's current filing checklist from the NAIC Annual Statement Instructions and the state department website, and note any state-specific supplement.
Have the Compliance Manager confirm the licence list is current, since a lapsed or newly granted licence changes the matrix.
checklist.done: the matrix carries one row per company per jurisdiction with method, opinion requirement, fee and checklist reference.

checklist.step: Take receipt of the signed opinion and check it before attachment
actions: Receive the signed opinion PDF from the Appointed Actuary and confirm it is text-searchable, unwatermarked and carries the signature block with name, title, address, telephone and email.
Check the opinion names the correct company, NAIC company code and valuation date, and that the signature date is on or before the intended filing date.
Compare the amounts quoted in the opinion to the exhibit values in the statutory reporting software and stop the filing on any difference.
Log receipt in the filing tracker with the file hash so the attached document can later be proven to be the signed one.
checklist.done: the signed opinion is verified against the statement figures and logged with a file hash before attachment.

checklist.step: Assemble the annual statement package
actions: Complete the annual statement blank: jurat page with officer signatures, Assets, Liabilities, Summary of Operations, Exhibits 5 through 8, Schedule S, Schedule T and the state pages.
Attach the signed Statement of Actuarial Opinion in the position the Annual Statement Instructions require, ahead of the notes to financial statements.
Attach the supplements due with the annual statement, including the Life Supplement, Schedule SIS where applicable and the Management Discussion and Analysis.
Have the Controller confirm the statement figures agree to the closed general ledger before the package is locked.
checklist.done: a complete blank with the signed opinion attached in the prescribed position is locked and agreed to the general ledger.

checklist.step: Clear the NAIC blanks cross-checks and validations
actions: Run the full validation suite in the statutory reporting software: crosschecks, edit checks and the NAIC electronic filing validations.
Clear every hard error; for each soft error or crosscheck warning left standing, write the explanation that will accompany the filing.
Confirm the actuarial opinion indicator fields on the jurat and the supplemental filing checklist are set to reflect that the opinion is attached.
Re-run the suite after every correction and keep the final clean validation report as evidence.
checklist.done: the final validation report shows zero hard errors and every remaining warning carries a written explanation.

checklist.step: Submit to the NAIC Financial Data Repository
actions: Generate the NAIC electronic filing file set from the statutory reporting software for the company and the annual period.
Upload the annual statement filing and the PDF filing to the NAIC Financial Data Repository through iSite+, selecting the correct filing type and period.
Confirm the repository acknowledges receipt and shows the filing status as accepted, and capture the submission timestamp and confirmation number.
Where the repository rejects the file, read the error report, correct in the source software and resubmit the same day rather than waiting for the next batch.
checklist.done: the NAIC filing shows an accepted status with a captured confirmation number and timestamp.

checklist.step: File with the Alaska Division of Insurance as domiciliary regulator
actions: Lodge the annual statement with the attached opinion with the Alaska Division of Insurance by 1 March, using the method the Division's current filing checklist specifies.
Include any Alaska-specific transmittal, the state page and the filing fee as scheduled in the Alaska checklist.
Where Alaska requires an original wet-signed opinion or jurat, arrange courier delivery with tracking so the delivery date is provable.
Capture the Division's acknowledgement and file it against the Alaska row of the jurisdiction matrix.
checklist.done: Alaska holds the statement with the attached opinion on or before 1 March, with an acknowledgement filed against the matrix row.

checklist.step: File with every non-domiciliary state of licensure
actions: Work the matrix state by state: for states that accept the NAIC filing alone, record the reliance and the NAIC confirmation number against the row.
For states requiring a direct lodgement, submit through that department's portal or by the method on its checklist, attaching the opinion where the state requires its own copy.
Complete each state's own supplements where required, such as the state page, premium tax reconciliation reference or the state-specific certification.
Record the submission date, method and reference on every row the same day it is filed, never in a catch-up batch.
checklist.done: every non-domiciliary row shows either a recorded NAIC reliance or a direct submission with date, method and reference.

checklist.step: File the RAAIS confidentially with the domiciliary commissioner
actions: Take the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary from the Appointed Actuary and confirm it is marked confidential on every page.
Lodge it with the Alaska Division of Insurance by 15 March through the channel the Division designates for confidential actuarial material.
Send the RAAIS to any other state that has requested it, and only where the state has requested it, recording the request in the matrix.
Capture the lodgement confirmation and set the tracker milestone to complete.
checklist.done: the RAAIS is lodged with the domiciliary commissioner on or before 15 March with a captured confirmation.

checklist.step: Pay the filing fees and reconcile them
actions: Take the fee column from the jurisdiction matrix and raise the payment run in the ERP for each state, by the method each state accepts (EFT, portal card payment or check).
Match every payment to a state row and record the payment reference and clearing date against it.
Chase any payment not cleared within 10 business days, since an unpaid fee can leave a filing formally incomplete.
Reconcile total fees paid to the matrix total and hand the reconciliation to the Controller.
checklist.done: every fee-bearing row shows a cleared payment reference and the total reconciles to the matrix.

checklist.step: Capture and index every filing confirmation
actions: Save each confirmation, acknowledgement email, portal receipt or courier proof of delivery as a PDF named <company>-<state>-annual-<year>.pdf.
Record the confirmation reference, timestamp and receiving system on the matrix row.
File all confirmations in the compliance evidence repository under the valuation year with a 7-year retention label.
Produce the confirmation register as a single export ready for an examiner request.
checklist.done: every filed row has a named, indexed confirmation PDF and a register export exists for the valuation year.

checklist.step: Work rejections and validation failures to closure
actions: Monitor the NAIC repository and state portal inboxes daily through March for rejection notices and data quality queries.
Log each rejection with the error code, the affected schedule or exhibit and the correcting action, and route actuarial errors straight to the Valuation Actuary.
Resubmit within 3 business days of the rejection and confirm the resubmission is accepted.
Escalate any rejection still open at 5 business days to the Chief Financial Officer.
checklist.done: every rejection is logged, corrected, resubmitted within 3 business days and confirmed accepted.

checklist.step: Handle any amended filing or re-issued opinion
actions: Where a reserve correction or an opinion re-issue is required after filing, agree the scope with the Appointed Actuary and Regulatory Counsel before anything is sent.
Prepare the amended annual statement with the amendment reason, file it to the NAIC and to every jurisdiction that received the original, and mark it clearly as amended.
Write the covering letter to the domiciliary commissioner explaining what changed and why, cleared by Regulatory Counsel and signed by the Chief Financial Officer.
Log the amendment in the tracker with the original and amended filing dates.
checklist.done: any amendment reaches every jurisdiction that got the original, with a counsel-cleared explanatory letter on file.

checklist.step: Reconcile the matrix to the confirmation register before closing the cycle
actions: Compare the jurisdiction matrix row by row to the confirmation register and list every row without a confirmation.
For each gap, establish whether the filing was made and the confirmation lost, or never made, and act on the same day.
Confirm that each row's confirmation timestamp is on or before the 1 March deadline, and compute days late where it is not.
Sign the reconciliation and hand it to the Chief Financial Officer as the filing completeness assertion.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation shows a dated confirmation for every matrix row, with days late computed for any that are not.

checklist.step: Report filing completeness to the audit committee
actions: Present the signed reconciliation, the count of jurisdictions filed on time, and any late or amended filings at the March audit committee meeting.
Report the opinion type filed and whether any state raised an immediate query on the opinion.
Record any committee direction on remediation in the minutes and assign owners.
Upload the minutes extract to the filing evidence pack.
checklist.done: the audit committee has seen filing completeness and any late filings, with directions minuted and owned.

checklist.step: Archive the filing pack for the valuation year
actions: Assemble the pack: filed statement PDFs by company, the attached signed opinion, the jurisdiction matrix, the confirmation register, fee reconciliation, rejection log and amendment file.
Index the pack by valuation year, company and state so a single state's filing can be produced without opening the whole pack.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the filing date and set the folder read-only.
Record the archive date and archiver on the pack cover sheet.
checklist.done: an indexed, read-only filing pack for the valuation year is archived under a 7-year retention label.

testing.step: Rebuild the filing population from the licence register
actions: Pull the certificate of authority list for every writing company independently from the company licence register, not from the filing matrix.
Build the expected population as company by jurisdiction, adding the NAIC as a filing destination in its own right.
Compare the rebuilt population to the jurisdiction matrix and treat any jurisdiction present in the licence register but absent from the matrix as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the rebuilt population reconciles to the filing matrix with every difference resolved or logged.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the confirmation register
actions: Match every population row to a confirmation PDF in the evidence repository on company, jurisdiction and valuation year.
Check each confirmation carries a system-generated reference and timestamp rather than an internal note asserting the filing was made.
List rows with no confirmation, or with an internally generated confirmation only, as exceptions before any sampling.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a system-generated confirmation or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of filings
actions: Take 100% of domiciliary filings and 100% of the NAIC submissions.
Take 15 non-domiciliary jurisdictions selected at random with a recorded seed, weighted to include every state that requires a direct lodgement.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and covers all domiciliary and NAIC filings.

testing.step: Re-perform the submission check in the NAIC repository
actions: Log in to iSite+ and open the Financial Data Repository filing history for each sampled company and the annual period.
Read the filing status, submission timestamp and confirmation number directly from the repository rather than from the internal register.
Compare the repository record to the confirmation PDF held internally and flag any difference in date or status.
Capture the repository filing history screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled NAIC filing is confirmed accepted directly in the repository, with the screen captured.

testing.step: Open the filed statement and prove the signed opinion is attached
actions: Open the filed PDF as lodged, not the internal draft, and locate the Statement of Actuarial Opinion in the position the Annual Statement Instructions require.
Check the attached opinion carries the signature, the signature date, the correct company name and NAIC company code and the correct valuation date.
Compare the file hash of the attached opinion to the hash logged when Regulatory Reporting received it from the Appointed Actuary.
Treat an unsigned, mismatched or absent opinion as an automatic fail regardless of whether the statement itself was accepted.
testing.done: each sampled filed statement contains the correct signed opinion, hash-matched to the one the Appointed Actuary issued.

testing.step: Test state-specific lodgement requirements on the sample
actions: Read each sampled state's current filing checklist from its department website and list what it demands beyond the NAIC filing.
Check the internal matrix row records the same requirements, and that any required original signature, state page, supplement or certification was actually sent.
For states that accept NAIC-only filing, confirm that reliance is stated in the state's own current instructions and not assumed from prior years.
Flag any row where the internal matrix is out of date against the published checklist.
testing.done: each sampled state's published checklist is matched to what was actually filed, with stale matrix rows flagged.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline maths for every sampled filing
actions: Compare each confirmation timestamp to the 1 March statutory deadline and compute days early or late, treating the state's own time zone as authoritative.
Compare the RAAIS lodgement date to 15 March and compute days early or late.
Where a deadline fell on a weekend or state holiday, check whether the state grants a next-business-day extension in its instructions before crediting it.
List every late filing with the number of days and the jurisdiction's late-filing penalty provision.
testing.done: every sampled filing has a computed timing result against its statutory deadline, with lateness quantified.

testing.step: Test fee payment and rejection closure
actions: Trace the fee for each sampled fee-bearing jurisdiction to a cleared payment in the ERP with a reference and clearing date.
Compare the amount paid to the fee published in the state's current fee schedule and flag any underpayment.
Pull the rejection log and confirm every rejection was resubmitted within 3 business days and confirmed accepted.
Treat any open rejection at the test date as a live filing failure rather than a housekeeping item.
testing.done: sampled fees trace to cleared payments at published amounts and no rejection remains open.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming company, jurisdiction, what was missed and whether the regulator is currently without a compliant filing.
Assign a root cause (stale licence list, matrix not refreshed against the state checklist, opinion received late, rejection not worked, fee unpaid) and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside 10 business days, and for any jurisdiction still unfiled, direct an immediate filing with a counsel-cleared covering letter.
Carry every open exception into the next annual cycle as a mandatory pre-filing check.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date, and no jurisdiction is left knowingly unfiled.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the filing test
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate and the count of jurisdictions with no confirmation against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with references to the confirmation register and the timing recomputation.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared and submitted none of the sampled filings, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the on-time rate and any unfiled jurisdiction to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the on-time filing rate, the exception count and a conclusion, with the committee reporting date recorded.
