checklist.step: Segment the in-force into testing blocks and record the basis
actions: Split the opinion scope into testing blocks by product family and risk profile: traditional life, universal life with secondary guarantees, deferred and payout annuities, variable annuities with guarantees, long-term care, disability income and deposit-type contracts.
For every block record the reserve amount at the valuation date and tie the sum of block reserves back to the Exhibit 5 through 8 totals produced by the Valuation Actuary.
Name and justify any block excluded from cash-flow testing, such as short-duration A&H, using the exclusion basis in ASOP 22, and quantify the reserve excluded.
Have the Chief Actuary approve the segmentation and the exclusion list before the run starts.
checklist.done: block reserves sum to the exhibit totals, every exclusion is justified and quantified, and the Chief Actuary has approved.

checklist.step: Assign assets to each testing block and reconcile them
actions: Extract the asset file at the valuation date by CUSIP with book value, market value, NAIC designation, coupon, maturity, call and prepayment features, and the investment segment code.
Map each investment segment to the liability testing block using the approved segmentation rules, and hand the mapping to the ALM actuary.
Reconcile total assigned book value to Schedule D, Schedule B, Schedule BA and the cash and short-term lines of the annual statement, and explain any unassigned asset.
Confirm with the Chief Investment Officer that segment-level assets are genuinely available to support the block rather than shared with another obligation.
checklist.done: assigned assets reconcile to Schedules D, B and BA with every unassigned asset explained and segment availability confirmed.

checklist.step: Set the reinvestment and disinvestment strategy to match what is actually done
actions: State the reinvestment strategy per block: asset mix, target quality, target duration and spread assumption, with the spread net of default cost and investment expense.
State the disinvestment order used when projected cash outflow exceeds inflow, naming which assets are sold first and at what market value basis.
Confirm in writing that the modelled strategy matches the current investment policy statement and current practice, and flag any deviation to the Appointed Actuary.
Provide the default cost assumption by NAIC designation and its source so the ALM actuary can evidence it.
checklist.done: a written, current reinvestment and disinvestment strategy with default costs by designation is signed by the CIO.

checklist.step: Generate and load the scenario sets
actions: Load the seven prescribed deterministic interest rate scenarios (level, up-down, pop-up, pop-down and the graded variants) with the starting yield curve as at the valuation date.
Generate the stochastic scenario set from the prescribed economic scenario generator for blocks tested stochastically, recording the generator version, seed and number of paths.
Load the equity return scenarios for variable annuity and equity-indexed blocks consistent with the VM-21 requirements.
Archive every scenario file with a hash so the exact scenarios can be reproduced at examination.
checklist.done: the deterministic, stochastic and equity scenario sets are loaded, versioned and hash-archived with the starting curve recorded.

checklist.step: Set moderately adverse assumption margins and document the rationale
actions: Start from the best-estimate mortality, morbidity, lapse, premium persistency, partial withdrawal and expense assumptions taken from the most recent experience studies, naming the study and its period.
Add the margin for moderately adverse deviation on each assumption and record the size of the margin and how it was set.

Give special treatment to the assumptions that drive the block: for long-term care apply the AG 51 sensitivity requirements, for secondary guarantee universal life focus on lapse and premium funding patterns.
Get Chief Actuary approval on each margin and lock the assumption set with a version tag before the run.
checklist.done: every assumption carries a named experience study, a documented margin and a dated Chief Actuary approval, locked under a version tag.

checklist.step: Apply Actuarial Guideline 53 to complex asset holdings
actions: Identify assets meeting the AG 53 definition of complex, including collateralised loan obligations, structured notes, private credit, affiliated investments and assets with projected returns above a public corporate benchmark.
For each, document the projected net investment return, the assumed default and expense costs and the evidence supporting a return in excess of the benchmark.
Run the AG 53 sensitivity that reduces excess returns on complex assets to the benchmark and record the reserve impact.
Prepare the AG 53 documentation and attestation content for inclusion in the actuarial memorandum.
checklist.done: complex assets are identified, their excess returns evidenced, the prescribed sensitivity run and the AG 53 documentation drafted.

checklist.step: Run the cash-flow projections
actions: Run each block over the full projection horizon, at least 30 years for life and annuity blocks and to run-off for long-term care, producing annual asset and liability cash flows.
Check the model reproduces the valuation-date starting reserve and starting asset book value before accepting the run.
Capture the ending surplus and the market value of surplus at the end of the horizon for every scenario, plus the year of first negative surplus where one occurs.
Clear every run log warning and rerun rather than accepting partial convergence.
checklist.done: every block runs to completion with the starting reserve and assets reproduced, and ending surplus captured per scenario.

checklist.step: Run the sensitivity suite
actions: Run the standard sensitivities: mortality and morbidity plus and minus, lapse plus and minus, expense inflation up, default cost doubled, and spread compression.
Run the AG 53 complex asset sensitivity and, for long-term care, the AG 51 required sensitivities including the morbidity improvement and rate increase assumptions.
Record for each sensitivity the change in ending surplus and whether the block moves from pass to fail.
Flag any assumption where a plausible movement flips the conclusion and take it to the Appointed Actuary as a material risk for the RAAIS.
checklist.done: the sensitivity suite is complete with the surplus impact of each and every conclusion-flipping assumption flagged.

checklist.step: Decide and document aggregation across blocks
actions: State whether results are aggregated across blocks and, if so, which blocks and on what basis, since aggregation can only reflect resources genuinely available across those blocks.
Compute results both aggregated and standalone and record the difference in the additional reserve.
Exclude from aggregation any block whose assets are ring-fenced, held in a separate account or committed to a specific obligation.
Sign the aggregation decision and pass both sets of results to the Appointed Actuary for the RAAIS disclosure.
checklist.done: the aggregation decision is signed, aggregated and standalone results are both computed and the difference is quantified.

checklist.step: Determine and book any additional reserve
actions: Identify every block with negative ending surplus under the prescribed deterministic scenarios or failing the stochastic measure.
Compute the additional reserve as the amount that restores non-negative ending surplus under the required measure, and document the method used.
Instruct the Statutory Reporting Manager to book the additional reserve in the correct exhibit line before the statement is locked.
Where no additional reserve is booked despite a failing scenario, state the reasoning in writing and obtain Chief Actuary sign-off, since this is the point examiners test hardest.
checklist.done: every failing block has a computed additional reserve booked, or a written, Chief Actuary approved reason it is not required.

checklist.step: Write the asset adequacy section of the actuarial memorandum
actions: Write up, per block: the reserve tested, the assets assigned and their reconciliation, the scenarios used, the assumptions and margins, the results, the sensitivities and the conclusion.
Include the AG 53 complex asset documentation and the AG 51 long-term care disclosures as separate labelled sections.
State the aggregation basis and its effect, and describe the reinvestment and disinvestment strategy signed by the CIO.
Cross-reference every stated result to the archived run output so an examiner can open the underlying file.
checklist.done: the memorandum's asset adequacy sections cover every block with cross-references to archived run output.

checklist.step: Put the AAT models through independent validation
actions: Confirm each cash-flow model carries a current validation report, and that any validation finding affecting the AAT result is disclosed to the Appointed Actuary.
Check the production model version used for the final run matches the approved release and that no post-freeze change was applied.
Review the static and dynamic validation evidence: starting balance reproduction, cash flow reasonableness checks and back-testing against actual experience.
Record the validation status per block and sign it.
checklist.done: every AAT model has a current validation status, an approved version on the final run and disclosed open findings.

checklist.step: Present the results to the risk committee
actions: Table the block-level results, the failing scenarios, the additional reserve and the assumptions most likely to flip the conclusion.
Compare aggregate surplus to the prior year and explain the movement in terms of new business, experience, assumption change and market conditions.
Record any committee direction on de-risking, reinsurance or asset repositioning in the minutes with owners.
Upload the minutes extract to the AAT evidence pack.
checklist.done: the risk committee has seen block results, the additional reserve and the year-on-year movement, with directions minuted.

checklist.step: Hand the AAT conclusion to the Appointed Actuary in writing
actions: Issue a dated conclusion memo by 31 January stating, block by block, whether reserves make good and sufficient provision under moderately adverse conditions.
Attach the results table, the sensitivity summary, the AG 53 and AG 51 sections and the aggregation statement.
State any limitation or unresolved item that would drive a qualified or inconclusive opinion so the Appointed Actuary is not surprised in February.
Obtain the Appointed Actuary's written acknowledgement of receipt.
checklist.done: a dated, acknowledged conclusion memo covering every block reaches the Appointed Actuary by 31 January.

checklist.step: Archive the AAT evidence pack
actions: Assemble the pack: segmentation and exclusion approval, asset segment file and reconciliation, CIO strategy statement, scenario files with hashes, assumption version tag, run logs, projection output, sensitivity results, aggregation decision, additional reserve calculation and validation status.
Index by valuation year and testing block so a single block can be produced on examiner request.
Apply the confidential-actuarial access label and the 7-year retention label from the valuation date.
Set the folder read-only and record the archive date.
checklist.done: an indexed, access-restricted, read-only AAT pack is archived under a 7-year retention label.

testing.step: Build the population of blocks requiring asset adequacy analysis
actions: Take the opinion scope table and list every reserve item in it, then map each to a testing block or to a documented exclusion.
Quantify the reserve tested and the reserve excluded, and compute the excluded reserve as a percentage of the total opinion scope.
Treat any reserve item that is neither tested nor covered by a written exclusion basis as an automatic exception before sampling.
testing.done: every opinion-scope reserve item maps to a tested block or a written exclusion, with excluded reserve quantified.

testing.step: Reconcile assigned assets to the filed investment schedules
actions: Total the book value of assets assigned across all testing blocks and compare to Schedule D Part 1, Schedule B, Schedule BA and the cash and short-term lines as filed.
List assets in the schedules that were assigned to no block and confirm they are genuinely surplus rather than quietly omitted support.
Check no asset is assigned to more than one block by matching CUSIPs across the block asset files.
Treat double-counted or missing assets as exceptions with the book value stated.
testing.done: assigned assets reconcile to the filed schedules with no CUSIP assigned twice and every unassigned asset explained.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of blocks and scenarios
actions: Take 100% of blocks with a booked additional reserve and 100% of blocks holding AG 53 complex assets or long-term care business.
Take three further blocks selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining tested population.
Within each sampled block, select all seven prescribed deterministic scenarios and, where stochastic, 10 paths for reproduction.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every additional-reserve, AG 53 and long-term care block.

testing.step: Reproduce the projection for the sampled blocks
actions: Re-run the archived model version against the hash-verified scenario files and the version-tagged assumption set for each sampled block.
Compare the reproduced ending surplus per scenario to the recorded result and treat any difference over 1% as an exception.
Confirm the run reproduces the valuation-date starting reserve and starting asset book value.
Attach the reproduction run log and the comparison table to the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled block reproduces its recorded ending surplus within 1% from archived scenarios and assumptions.

testing.step: Verify the scenario sets against the prescribed requirements
actions: Check the seven deterministic scenarios match the prescribed shapes and that the starting yield curve equals the published curve at the valuation date.
For stochastic blocks, confirm the economic scenario generator version, calibration date and path count meet the Valuation Manual requirements and that the recorded seed reproduces the same paths.
Confirm the equity scenarios used for variable annuity and indexed blocks are consistent with VM-21.
Flag any scenario file whose hash does not match the archived record as an evidence integrity exception.
testing.done: sampled scenario sets match the prescribed shapes, calibration and path count, and every file hash reconciles.

testing.step: Challenge the assumption margins against experience
actions: For each sampled block, read the named experience study and compare the best-estimate assumption used to the study result, including the study period and credibility.
Check the margin for moderately adverse deviation is documented, quantified and directionally correct on every assumption.
Compare the actual experience of the last two years to the assumption and flag any assumption that experience has already breached.
Treat an assumption with no experience study, no margin, or a margin set only by reference to last year as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled assumption traces to an experience study with a quantified margin that current experience does not already breach.

testing.step: Test that the modelled investment strategy matches the executed one
actions: Read the CIO strategy statement used in the model and compare it to the current investment policy statement approved by the board.
Pull actual purchases over the last four quarters from the investment system and compare the realised asset mix, quality and duration to the modelled reinvestment assumption.
Compare the modelled spread net of default cost to actual new-money spreads achieved and to the default cost assumption by NAIC designation.
Treat a material gap between modelled and executed strategy as a fail, since it undermines every projection built on it.
testing.done: the modelled reinvestment mix, quality, duration and spread are corroborated by actual purchase activity and the board policy.

testing.step: Recompute the additional reserve and the aggregation effect
actions: For each block with negative ending surplus, recompute the additional reserve needed to restore non-negative surplus under the required measure.
Compare the recomputed amount to the amount booked and trace the booked amount to the exhibit line and the valuation journal entry.
Recompute the standalone versus aggregated result and confirm the RAAIS discloses the aggregation effect accurately.
Treat any failing block with no booked reserve and no Chief Actuary approved written reasoning as a reportable finding, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: recomputed additional reserves agree to booked amounts and the disclosed aggregation effect reconciles.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the block, the reserve affected and whether the opinion conclusion depends on the disputed item.
Assign a root cause (untested block, asset double-count, stale assumption, strategy mismatch, missing AG 53 support, unbooked additional reserve) and an owner.
Where the finding would change the opinion, notify the Appointed Actuary the same day and set a remediation date before the 1 March filing.
Carry every open exception into next year's AAT cycle as a mandatory pre-run check.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date, with opinion-relevant findings escalated same day.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the asset adequacy review
actions: Compute the exception count and the aggregate reserve impact against the requirement that every in-scope block be tested and every failing block reserved.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with references to the reproduction runs and the asset reconciliation.
Have the independent reviewer, who parameterised and ran none of the sampled projections, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any unreserved failing block to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the model governance repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception count, the reserve impact and a conclusion, with the committee reporting date recorded.

checklist.step: Pull the independent source-of-record control totals
actions: Run the standard in-force control report directly in the policy administration system as at the quarter end, producing policy count, face amount, account value and annualised premium by plan code and status.
Run it from the system's own reporting layer, not from a warehouse table, so the figure is genuinely independent of the extract being tested.
Include terminated-this-quarter policies as a separate line so lapses and deaths can be reconciled rather than silently disappearing.
Sign and timestamp the report and send it to the Data Quality Manager the same day.
checklist.done: a signed, timestamped source-of-record control report by plan code is with the Data Quality Manager.

checklist.step: Take the warehouse extract control totals
actions: Query the loaded valuation extract table for the quarter end and produce the same control totals by plan code and status.
Record the pipeline run id, the load timestamp and the row counts at each stage (landed, transformed, published) from the orchestration log.
List every row rejected by the load with its rejection reason, since rejected rows are the most common cause of a silent shortfall.
Hand both control totals and the rejection listing to the Data Quality Manager.
checklist.done: warehouse control totals, stage row counts and the rejection listing are delivered with the pipeline run id.

checklist.step: Take the model in-force control totals
actions: Produce the model in-force summary from the valuation run: records loaded, records modelled, records failed, and control totals by plan code.
Report separately any policy the model grouped, compressed or mapped to a proxy plan, with the count and face amount involved.
Confirm the model in-force date matches the reconciliation quarter end exactly.
Deliver the summary and the failed-record listing to the Data Quality Manager.
checklist.done: model in-force control totals, grouping treatment and failed-record listing are delivered for the correct valuation date.

checklist.step: Perform the three-way tie by plan code
actions: Lay the three sets of control totals side by side by plan code: policy admin, warehouse extract, model in-force.
Compute the difference between each pair on policy count, face amount, account value and premium, in absolute and percentage terms.
Apply the tolerance table: exact tie on policy count, 0.1% by plan code and 0.01% in aggregate on values.
Highlight every plan code outside tolerance and every plan code present in one system and absent in another.
checklist.done: a three-way tie sheet exists by plan code with tolerance results and missing plan codes highlighted.

checklist.step: Explain every reconciling item and assign it an owner
actions: For each out-of-tolerance difference, drive it to a named cause: timing of a post-cut transaction, extract filter, rejected rows, plan remap, model grouping, or a genuine data defect.
Quantify the reserve impact of each item with the Valuation Actuary, and mark it as reserve-affecting or presentational.
Name an owner and a target resolution date on every item, and record the quarter in which it first appeared so ageing is visible.
Refuse to close an item with a description of the difference in place of a cause.
checklist.done: every reconciling item has a named cause, a quantified reserve impact, an owner, a target date and a first-appeared quarter.

checklist.step: Reconcile the reserve control totals to the general ledger
actions: Take the model reserve totals by segment and compare them to the reserve account balances in the general ledger trial balance at quarter end.
Bridge the difference through the valuation journal entry, manual reserve adjustments and any reserve held outside the model.
List every manual adjustment with its preparer, approver, amount and supporting memo, since unsupported manual reserve entries are an examination magnet.
Confirm the reserve totals agree to the exhibit lines about to be reported.
checklist.done: model reserves, the general ledger reserve accounts and the exhibit lines agree, with every manual adjustment supported.

checklist.step: Account for off-system and closed blocks
actions: Maintain the schedule of blocks not held in the main policy administration system: acquired closed blocks, spreadsheet-administered legacy plans, third-party administered business and assumed reinsurance.
For each, name the source of record, the control total received, who produced it and the date, and obtain a signed certification from the third-party administrator where one holds the records.
Reconcile each off-system block's reserve to the exhibit line it feeds and show it separately on the reconciliation.
Flag any off-system block with no independent control total as an unsupported reserve to the Appointed Actuary.
checklist.done: every off-system block has a named source of record, a dated control total or TPA certification, and a reserve reconciled to its exhibit line.

checklist.step: Reconcile the movement quarter on quarter
actions: Build the in-force movement: opening count and face amount, new business issued, deaths, surrenders, lapses, maturities, conversions, reinstatements, closing count and face amount.
Tie the movement to the new business register from Underwriting and to the claims register from Claims, rather than accepting the extract's own movement figures.
Explain any closing balance that does not equal opening plus movement, and treat an unexplained gap as a defect in the extract not in the arithmetic.
Compare the movement rates to the prior four quarters and query any rate outside historical range with Policy Administration.
checklist.done: opening plus movement equals closing by plan code, tied to the new business and claims registers, with rate outliers queried.

checklist.step: Test the critical valuation fields, not just the totals
actions: Select 25 policies per major plan code and compare, field by field, the policy admin screen values to the extract row: issue date, issue age, sex, plan code, face amount, mode, paid-to date, rider set, account value and reinsurance indicator.
Record each mismatch with the field name, since a matching total can still hide offsetting field-level errors that change the reserve.
Test the reinsurance indicator specifically against the treaty repository, because a wrong cession flag moves reserve credit.
Report field-level accuracy by plan code alongside the control total tie.
checklist.done: field-level accuracy is measured on a per-policy comparison and reported alongside the control totals.

checklist.step: Clear the suspense and unapplied items
actions: Pull the suspense, unapplied cash and pending transaction queues at quarter end with counts, values and ageing.
Post everything that can be posted before the extract cut and provide the residual balance with an explanation of why each item cannot yet be posted.
Quantify the reserve effect of unposted items with the Valuation Actuary, and disclose it on the reconciliation if it is material.
Set a clearance target for items aged over 60 days and report progress at the next close.
checklist.done: the residual suspense balance is quantified, its reserve effect disclosed and items over 60 days have a clearance target.

checklist.step: Write the ASOP 23 data reliance summary
actions: Summarise for the Appointed Actuary: records supplied, records rejected and why, records corrected, residual population valued, field-level accuracy results and every unresolved reconciling item with its reserve impact.
State whether the data are sufficiently accurate and complete for the intended valuation purpose, and name any limitation the actuary must disclose.
Attach the signed three-way tie sheet and the reserve to general ledger reconciliation as support.
Deliver it before the officer signs the data reliance statement, not afterwards.
checklist.done: a signed ASOP 23 summary with a sufficiency statement and named limitations reaches the Appointed Actuary before the reliance statement is signed.

checklist.step: Sign off the reconciliation
actions: Review the three-way tie, the reconciling item schedule with ageing and the field-level accuracy result.
Challenge any item recurring for more than two quarters and require a permanent fix ticket rather than a repeat manual adjustment.
Sign and date the reconciliation jointly with the Chief Actuary where a reserve is affected.
Release the extract for the valuation run only once the signature is in place.
checklist.done: the reconciliation is signed and dated, repeat items carry permanent fix tickets, and the extract is released for valuation.

checklist.step: Raise permanent fixes into the data backlog
actions: Convert every recurring reconciling item into a backlog ticket with the plan codes affected, the reserve impact and the system change required.
Assign the ticket to the owning platform team with the next policy administration or pipeline release as the target.
Add a regression check to the release so the same defect cannot return unnoticed.
Report open data defect count and ageing to the data governance forum each quarter.
checklist.done: each recurring item has a backlog ticket with a target release and a regression check, and open defects are reported to the governance forum.

checklist.step: Refresh the lineage and the extract specification
actions: Update the documented lineage from policy administration fields through the pipeline transformations to the model input fields in the data catalog.
Version the extract specification whenever a filter, join or derivation changes, and record who approved the change and when.
Confirm the specification the pipeline actually executes matches the published version, since drift between the two is what produces silent shortfalls.
Publish the refreshed lineage to Actuarial before the next quarter close.
checklist.done: published lineage and a versioned extract specification match what the pipeline executes, with approvals recorded.

checklist.step: Archive the reconciliation pack
actions: Assemble the pack: source control report, warehouse totals with pipeline run id, model in-force summary, three-way tie sheet, reconciling item schedule, general ledger reconciliation, off-system block schedule, field-level accuracy results and the signed ASOP 23 summary.
Index by quarter end and plan code so a single plan can be produced on request.
Apply the 7-year retention label running from the valuation date.
Set read-only and record the archive date and archiver.
checklist.done: an indexed, read-only reconciliation pack is archived for the quarter under a 7-year retention label.

testing.step: Rebuild the population of plan codes feeding the valuation
actions: Pull the full plan code master from the policy administration system, including plans closed to new business but still in force.
Compare it to the plan codes appearing in the reconciliation and list any plan present in the master but absent from the reconciliation.
Add the off-system block schedule so third-party administered and legacy blocks are inside the population, not alongside it.
Treat any in-force plan code absent from the reconciliation as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the population covers every in-force plan code and off-system block, with omissions logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Re-extract the source control totals independently
actions: Run the in-force control report in the policy administration system with your own credentials as at the same quarter end.
Compare your figures to the source control report used in the reconciliation and investigate any difference, including report parameter differences.
Confirm the report was run against production and not a reporting copy with a different cut time.
Capture the report parameters and output into the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently run source control report agrees to the one used in the reconciliation, with parameters captured.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of plan codes outside tolerance and 100% of off-system blocks.
Take 10 plan codes selected at random with a recorded seed from those that tied, plus 25 individual policies across them for field-level testing.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every out-of-tolerance plan code and every off-system block.

testing.step: Re-perform the three-way tie on the sample
actions: Query the warehouse extract table yourself for the sampled plan codes and produce control totals without using the reconciliation workbook.
Pull the model in-force totals for the same plan codes from the archived valuation run output.
Compare all three sets and apply the published tolerance table independently.
Flag any plan code the reconciliation reported as tying that does not tie on re-performance.
testing.done: the three-way tie is independently reproduced for every sampled plan code with tolerance applied.

testing.step: Test field-level accuracy against the source screens
actions: Open each sampled policy in the policy administration system and read issue date, issue age, sex, plan code, face amount, paid-to date, rider set, account value and reinsurance indicator from the screen.
Compare each field to the extract row and to the model input record, recording mismatches by field name.
Recompute the reserve effect of any mismatched valuation-driving field with the Valuation Actuary.
Treat a mismatched issue date, issue age, plan code or reinsurance indicator as a reserve-affecting exception even where totals tie.
testing.done: sampled policies are field-matched to the source screens with the reserve effect of every mismatch quantified.

testing.step: Age the reconciling items and test their causes
actions: Pull the reconciling item schedule for the last four quarters and identify every item present in more than one quarter.
Read the stated cause for each and confirm it names a mechanism, not a restatement of the difference.
Check each recurring item has a backlog ticket with a target release, and confirm the release actually shipped where the target date has passed.
Treat any item aged beyond one quarter without a fix ticket as a fail.
testing.done: every recurring reconciling item has a mechanism-level cause and a live fix ticket, or is logged as a fail.

testing.step: Trace the reserve control totals to the ledger and the exhibits
actions: Trace the model reserve totals for sampled segments to the general ledger reserve account balances at quarter end.
Pull every manual reserve journal in the quarter and test that each has a preparer, an independent approver and a supporting memo.
Compare the reconciled reserve to the exhibit lines as reported in the quarterly or annual statement.
Flag any manual reserve journal without independent approval as a control failure regardless of amount.
testing.done: sampled reserves tie from model to ledger to exhibit and every manual journal is independently approved and supported.

testing.step: Test off-system block support and third-party certifications
actions: For each off-system block, obtain the control total and the third-party administrator certification used, and check it is signed, dated and covers the correct period.
Where a TPA holds the records, check whether a service organisation control report exists covering the period and read its exceptions.
Recompute the block reserve from the supplied control total on the prescribed basis and compare to the amount booked.
Treat any off-system block supported only by a spreadsheet with no independent certification as a fail.
testing.done: every off-system block has a signed, period-correct certification and a reserve recomputed from an independent control total.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the plan code or block, the field or total affected and the quantified reserve impact.
Assign a root cause (extract filter, rejected rows, plan remap, model grouping, unposted suspense, uncertified off-system block) and an owner.
Where the exception affects a reserve in a filed statement, notify the Appointed Actuary and the Statutory Reporting Manager the same day.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly reconciliation as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date, with filed-statement impacts escalated same day.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the reconciliation test
actions: Compute the proportion of plan codes tying within tolerance, the field-level accuracy rate and the aggregate reserve impact of open items.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with references to the re-performed tie and the field-level testing.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither produced the extract nor prepared the reconciliation, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any reserve-affecting data defect to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the tie rate, field accuracy, reserve impact and a conclusion, with the committee reporting date recorded.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Actuarial memorandum delivered within 30 days of a commissioner request under the AOMR; all other inquiries answered by the date stated in the department letter, defaulting to 10 business days where none is stated; examination information requests answered by the examiner's stated due date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Tracker reminders at 50% and 80% of the elapsed response window, plus a daily reminder in the final 3 days, escalating to the Chief Financial Officer if the due date is reached without a cleared draft

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Inbound letter, intake record, evidence index, drafts, counsel clearance, the submitted response and the department acknowledgement retained 7 years from closure, indexed by jurisdiction and valuation year

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any inquiry answered after its due date, answered without counsel clearance, or answered with information later corrected is logged as an exception with the correction sent and the owner

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off every corrected or supplemental response to a regulator and any release of confidential actuarial material

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every valuation-related inquiry received in the period from any state department or examiner, including memorandum requests, financial analyst questions, examination information requests and follow-ups

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — a response sent after the due date, without counsel clearance, or containing a statement not supported by the archived valuation evidence is a fail; one fail escalates to the CFO

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; the test runs quarterly over every inquiry closed in the quarter, with 100% coverage rather than sampling given the low volume

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted, cleared or submitted any tested response

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly regulator inquiry test workpaper (inquiry register, due date recomputation, clearance evidence, statement tracing) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Inquiry register with inbound date, due date, submission date and acknowledgement per jurisdiction, producible to an examiner within 3 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting is the single channel to the department; the Appointed Actuary drafts actuarial content, Regulatory Counsel clears and asserts AOMR confidentiality, and no one else corresponds with the regulator directly

checklist.step: Take in the inquiry and log it the day it arrives
actions: Monitor the regulatory mailbox, the department portals and the examiner's information request list daily, and capture every inbound valuation item the same day.
Create a tracker record with jurisdiction, department contact, receipt date, the exact question text, the stated due date and the statutory hook where one is cited.
Classify the inquiry: memorandum request under the AOMR, financial analyst question from the Financial Analysis Handbook review, examination information request, or opinion follow-up.
Notify the Appointed Actuary, the Regulatory Reporting Manager and Regulatory Counsel within one business day of receipt.
checklist.done: a tracker record exists with jurisdiction, receipt date, question text, due date and classification, and the actuary and counsel are notified.

checklist.step: Compute the response due date and arm the reminders
actions: Use the due date stated in the department letter where one is given; where none is given, apply the 30-day statutory window for an AOMR memorandum request and 10 business days otherwise.
Check whether the stated period runs in calendar or business days and whether it starts from the letter date or the receipt date, and record which reading was applied.
Set the tracker reminders at 50% and 80% of the window and daily in the final 3 days.
Where the window is not achievable, request an extension in writing before the due date rather than after it, and file the department's reply.
checklist.done: a computed due date with its day-count basis is recorded, reminders are armed, and any extension is requested in writing before the deadline.

checklist.step: Assess confidentiality before anything is assembled
actions: Determine whether the material requested is the actuarial memorandum, the RAAIS or supporting workpapers, each of which carries confidential treatment under the AOMR.
Draft the confidentiality assertion to accompany the production, naming the statutory provision in the requesting state that protects it.
Confirm the requester is the domiciliary commissioner or an authorised examiner where the material is confidential, and check the authority of any non-domiciliary requester before releasing.
Record the confidentiality decision on the tracker record so it governs how the material is transmitted.
checklist.done: a written confidentiality position naming the protecting provision is recorded before any material is assembled.

checklist.step: Assemble the evidence from the archived packs
actions: Pull from the archived valuation pack the seriatim output, valuation basis inventory, roll-forward and exhibit tie-out for the years in question.
Pull from the AAT pack the scenario files, block results, sensitivity summary and additional reserve calculation.
Pull the signed opinion, memorandum, RAAIS and reliance statements from the opinion pack.
Build an evidence index mapping each element of the question to the specific document, page and figure that answers it, and hand it to the Appointed Actuary.
checklist.done: an evidence index maps every element of the question to a named document, page and figure from the archived packs.

checklist.step: Draft the actuarial response
actions: Answer the question actually asked, in the order asked, restating each question before its answer so the analyst can follow it without cross-referencing.
Support every numerical statement with a reference to the evidence index entry behind it, and attach the referenced exhibit rather than describing it.
Where the answer discloses a weakness, state it plainly with the remediation already in train, since a discovered omission costs far more than a disclosed one.
Keep the response within the scope of the question and do not volunteer unrelated material that widens the inquiry.
checklist.done: a draft answers each question in order with every figure tied to an evidence index reference and attachments included.

checklist.step: Have the drafting reviewed by the Chief Actuary
actions: Read the draft against the question text and confirm nothing asked has been left unanswered or partly answered.
Check every figure against the attached evidence and confirm consistency with what was filed in the opinion, memorandum and annual statement.
Challenge any statement that goes further than the evidence supports, and any characterisation of methodology not reflected in the workpapers.
Record review comments and their disposition on the tracker record.
checklist.done: the Chief Actuary has recorded a completed review with every comment dispositioned before counsel clearance.

checklist.step: Obtain Regulatory Counsel clearance
actions: Review the draft for admissions, privilege issues and statements that could be read as conceding a reserve deficiency or a statutory breach.
Attach the confidentiality assertion drafted earlier and confirm the transmission method protects it.
Confirm the response does not conflict with any position taken in another jurisdiction on the same facts, checking the inquiry register for parallel questions.
Record dated clearance in the legal document system and on the tracker record; no response leaves without it.
checklist.done: dated counsel clearance with the confidentiality assertion attached is recorded against the tracker record.

checklist.step: Obtain officer approval for the response
actions: Review responses that touch reserve adequacy, an additional reserve, a qualified opinion or a restatement, and approve them in writing.
Confirm the response is consistent with what has been told to the board and the audit committee.
Where the response reveals an issue not yet reported internally, direct that it goes to the audit committee before or with the submission.
Record the approval and date on the tracker record.
checklist.done: reserve-adequacy responses carry a dated CFO approval consistent with board reporting.

checklist.step: Submit through the single regulatory channel
actions: Send the response through the channel the department specified: the department portal, the examiner's secure information request system, or the named analyst by secure email.
Include the covering letter with the company name, NAIC company code, valuation year, the department's reference number and the confidentiality assertion.
Confirm attachments open, are text-searchable and are complete, since a corrupted or partial attachment restarts the clock in practice even if not in law.
Capture the submission timestamp and any portal confirmation number on the tracker record.
checklist.done: the response is submitted through the specified channel with a captured timestamp and confirmation reference.

checklist.step: Handle the memorandum production request specifically
actions: Where the commissioner requests the actuarial memorandum, produce the memorandum as completed, plus any supporting workpapers the request names, within the 30-day window.
Confirm the memorandum version produced is the one supporting the opinion for the valuation year requested, not a later revision.
Attach the confidentiality assertion and record that the memorandum was released, to whom and on what date, on the opinion pack cover sheet.
Offer a walkthrough call with the analyst, since a 30-minute call frequently closes an inquiry that would otherwise run for months.
checklist.done: the correct-year memorandum is produced within 30 days under a confidentiality assertion, with the release recorded on the opinion pack.

checklist.step: Work follow-up questions and examination information requests
actions: Log each follow-up as its own tracker record linked to the parent inquiry, with its own due date, rather than appending it to a closed record.
For examination information requests, maintain the running request list with request number, description, owner, due date and status, and reconcile it to the examiner's own list weekly.
Escalate any request that would require new analysis rather than retrieval to the Chief Actuary immediately, since these are what cause overruns.
Report the open request count and ageing to the Chief Financial Officer weekly during an examination.
checklist.done: every follow-up has its own dated record, the examination request list reconciles weekly, and open ageing is reported.

checklist.step: Correct anything that turns out to be wrong
actions: Where a submitted answer is later found to be inaccurate, prepare a correction the same week it is discovered, stating what was wrong, the correct position and how it happened.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the correction and the Chief Financial Officer approve it before it is sent.
Send the correction to every jurisdiction that received the original answer, not only the one that noticed.
Log the correction against the original tracker record with the discovery date, submission date and root cause.
checklist.done: every discovered inaccuracy is corrected to all recipients within the week, cleared by counsel and logged with a root cause.

checklist.step: Close the inquiry on evidence, not assumption
actions: Obtain the department acknowledgement, a closure email, or the examiner's confirmation that the request is satisfied, and attach it to the tracker record.
Where no acknowledgement comes, follow up at 15 business days and record the follow-up rather than closing on silence.
Record the outcome: satisfied, satisfied with follow-up, or escalated to a formal finding.
Set the record to closed only once acknowledgement or a documented follow-up sits on it.
checklist.done: each inquiry is closed against an acknowledgement or a documented follow-up, with the outcome recorded.

checklist.step: Feed the lessons back into the valuation process
actions: Review closed inquiries each quarter and identify what the regulator repeatedly asks about, by topic and jurisdiction.
Where a question recurs, add the answer and its supporting exhibit to the standard memorandum content so the next year's filing pre-empts it.
Raise process changes where an inquiry exposed a documentation or evidence gap, with an owner and a target valuation cycle.
Report inquiry themes and any repeat topic to the audit committee annually.
checklist.done: recurring inquiry topics are pre-empted in the memorandum content and any evidence gap has an owned process change.

checklist.step: Archive the correspondence file
actions: Assemble per inquiry: the inbound letter, the intake record, the evidence index, drafts, Chief Actuary review, counsel clearance, CFO approval, the submitted response with attachments and the acknowledgement.
Index by jurisdiction, valuation year and department reference number so a state's whole correspondence history is retrievable in one query.
Apply the confidential label where the memorandum or RAAIS was released, and the 7-year retention label from closure.
Set read-only and record the archive date.
checklist.done: an indexed, read-only correspondence file per inquiry is archived by jurisdiction and valuation year under a 7-year retention label.

testing.step: Build the population of valuation inquiries received in the quarter
actions: Extract every inquiry record classified as valuation-related in the quarter with jurisdiction, receipt date, due date, submission date and status.
Search the regulatory mailbox and the department portals independently for inbound items in the same period and compare to the tracker.
Add examination information requests from the examiner's own request list so exam traffic is inside the population.
Treat any inbound item found in the mailbox or portal but absent from the tracker as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the tracker population reconciles to an independent mailbox, portal and examiner-list sweep with every gap logged.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the regulator's own record
actions: For each department that raised more than one inquiry, compare the internal register to the department's correspondence or portal history for the period.
Confirm each internal record carries the department's reference number so the two lists can be matched item by item.
List any item the department shows as open that the internal register shows as closed, and treat it as a live exception.
Capture the department history screens or letters relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: the internal register matches the department's own record item by item, with any regulator-open item flagged.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of inquiries in the quarter given the low volume, and all follow-ups linked to them.
Within each, select every numerical statement in the submitted response for tracing, plus the confidentiality decision and the clearance evidence.
Record the selection basis, the period covered and the extraction date in the workpaper.
testing.done: all inquiries and follow-ups in the quarter are in scope, with statements, confidentiality and clearance selected for testing.

testing.step: Recompute every response deadline
actions: Read each inbound letter and recompute the due date from the date stated on its face, applying the day-count basis the letter uses.
For memorandum production requests, recompute the 30-day window under the AOMR and check the delivery date against it.
Where no due date was stated, confirm the internal 10-business-day default was applied and met.
Compare each recomputed due date to the submission timestamp and record days early or late for every item.
testing.done: each inquiry has an independently recomputed due date and a timing result stated in days against the submission.

testing.step: Trace every numerical statement to archived evidence
actions: Take each figure quoted in the submitted responses and locate it in the archived valuation, AAT or opinion pack using the evidence index.
Confirm the figure matches the archived source exactly and that the source pre-dates the response.
Check the figure is consistent with what was filed in the opinion, the memorandum and the annual statement for the same year.
Treat any figure with no traceable source, or one inconsistent with a filed document, as a reportable finding.
testing.done: every quoted figure traces to a pre-dating archived source and agrees with the filed documents.

testing.step: Test counsel clearance and officer approval
actions: For each response, confirm a dated Regulatory Counsel clearance exists and pre-dates the submission timestamp.
For responses touching reserve adequacy, an additional reserve or a qualified opinion, confirm a dated Chief Financial Officer approval also pre-dates submission.
Confirm the Chief Actuary review sheet exists with comments dispositioned.
Treat clearance dated after submission as equivalent to no clearance at all.
testing.done: every submission has counsel clearance, and where required officer approval, dated before the submission timestamp.

testing.step: Test the confidentiality handling of released actuarial material
actions: Identify every response that released the actuarial memorandum, the RAAIS or supporting workpapers.
Confirm a confidentiality assertion naming the protecting statutory provision accompanied each release and that the transmission channel was secure.
Confirm the requester was the domiciliary commissioner or an authorised examiner, and that any non-domiciliary release was authority-checked before sending.
Confirm the release is recorded on the opinion pack cover sheet with recipient and date.
testing.done: every release of confidential actuarial material was authority-checked, assertion-covered, securely sent and recorded.

testing.step: Test closure evidence and corrections
actions: For each closed record, open the attached acknowledgement or documented follow-up and confirm it relates to the inquiry and post-dates the submission.
Identify any record closed on silence with no follow-up at 15 business days and log it.
For any correction sent during the period, confirm it reached every jurisdiction that received the original and carried counsel clearance and CFO approval.
Record the discovery-to-correction elapsed days for each correction.
testing.done: every closure rests on a dated acknowledgement or follow-up, and corrections reached all original recipients with clearance.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the jurisdiction, the inquiry reference, what failed and whether the regulator is currently holding an unanswered or inaccurate response.
Assign a root cause (intake missed the item, due date miscomputed, evidence not retrievable, clearance bypassed, closed on silence, untraceable figure) and an owner.
Where a regulator holds an inaccurate answer, direct a corrected submission within 5 business days with counsel clearance.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date, and any inaccurate answer is corrected within 5 business days.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the inquiry response test
actions: Compute the on-time response rate, the clearance compliance rate and the count of untraceable statements against the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with references to the deadline recomputation and the statement tracing.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted, cleared or submitted none of the tested responses, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any regulator-held inaccuracy to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the on-time rate, clearance rate, untraceable-statement count and a conclusion, with the committee reporting date recorded.
